title: Once a Week, a Sloth Risks Its Life to Poop

scenes.text: Once a week, a sloth risks its life to poop.
It climbs all the way down from the treetops, slow as ever.
Each trip, it can lose a fifth of its body weight.
On the ground, researchers estimate about half of sloths get killed by predators.
Why risk it? One idea: moths in its fur lay eggs in the droppings, which feeds the algae that camouflage the sloth.
But captive sloths still make the trip. Once a week. Nobody knows why.

description:
Once a week, a sloth risks its life to poop.
Brown-throated three-toed sloths climb down from the canopy about once a week, and the trip costs them a fifth of their body weight in poop and a lot of energy.
Why do you think they do it? Comment below.
first_comment: Would you climb down a tree every week if half of the trips ended badly?
